A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LV-XAttn by the same authors. Their main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original distributed runtime measurements, comparisons with Ring Attention and DeepSpeed-Ulysses, and communication-overlap and activation-recomputation ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Llama 3-V runtime measurements on both principal GPU configurations.

M1.justification: The documented forward procedure replaces separately exchanged and rescaled m and l softmax statistics with a single L statistic in Algorithm 1. This changes the specified communicated state, while local KV storage, query/output rotation, communication overlap, and activation recomputation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: No new dataset, domain, or task is evaluated. Llama 3-V extends model configurations for the existing distributed cross-attention timing workload. Video-MME remains an input-size motivation, and the new hybrid-architecture discussion does not report evaluations.

E2.justification: Ring Attention and DeepSpeed-Ulysses retain their roles in the runtime comparisons. v3 Section 4.1 additionally reports comparing LV-XAttn outputs against PyTorch scaled dot-product attention as a correctness reference, rather than a new speed baseline.

E3.justification: Tables 2–4 add Llama 3-V-11b, with eight cross-attention layers, 40 LM blocks, and model-specific text/frame configurations on the existing A100 and A30 clusters. Existing model configurations, batch size, hardware setups, and timing metrics are retained. Random-input benchmarking is newly disclosed, not established as a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 2 extends the runtime-breakdown analysis to Llama 3-V, and Section 4.1 newly reports output agreement with PyTorch attention. The communication-overlap and activation-recomputation ablations in Figures 5 and 6 retain their experimental comparisons and plotted results.

E5.justification: v3 Section 4.1 first states that runtimes are averaged over five trials after two warmup runs. v1 provides no corresponding trial-count or averaging disclosure. This does not establish increased repetition; neither version reports dispersion estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 4 add a complete Llama 3-V comparison across both principal clusters, including 7.51–10.62× total speedups on A100 and 2.2–3.13× on A30. All existing numerical rows in Tables 3–6 are retained. Several summaries are corrected, including the DeepSpeed-Ulysses speedup range from 1.21–1.55× to 1.34–1.55× and the Figure 6 capacity multipliers to 1.5× for mPLUG and 1.6× for OpenFlamingo. The higher headline speedup comes from added model results, not improved performance under an existing setting.

T1.justification: Equation 1 revises communicated volume from 3SQd/n + SQ/n to 2SQd/n + SQ/n. Appendix A correspondingly changes the approximate favorable condition from SKV > 1.5SQ to SKV > SQ, restores a missing d factor in Ring Attention's communication volume, and updates Figure 7. These are limited revisions to the existing runtime analysis; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the evaluated-model claim to Llama 3-V and raise the reported maximum end-to-end speedup from 5.58× to 10.62×. The introduction's communication-volume example changes from 0.48% for mPLUG-Owl3 to 0.04% for Llama 3-V. The core contributions of exact distributed cross-attention and memory-saving recomputation remain.

C2.justification: The new Discussion expands the existing architecture comparison and explicitly argues that LV-XAttn also applies to hybrid concatenation/cross-attention models. The A30 interpretation additionally attributes weaker end-to-end gains to lower GPU FLOPS alongside slower interconnects. Appendix A retains the qualification favoring Ring Attention for self-attention.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and identifies PyTorch, torch.distributed, Triton rescaling kernels, and publicly available model checkpoints. It also discloses randomly generated benchmark inputs, warmup runs, and the input sizes used in Figure 2. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments; repository accessibility was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to NVLM, ModServe, and Triton. NVLM and ModServe support expanded positioning around architectural efficiency and hybrid models, while Triton supports implementation documentation. The existing attention and parallelism literature and principal novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: The MLLM architecture discussion moves from Related Work into an expanded Discussion section. v3 also adds implementation and benchmarking paragraphs, an Impact Statement, and targeted wording and terminology corrections. Most of the narrative and section organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains a Llama panel and a fuller caption; Figure 4 adds Llama markers, a larger vertical range, and an inset; Figure 7 is enlarged and redrawn with revised boundaries. Tables 2–4 gain Llama rows, and Algorithm 1 and existing figures are relocated. The overall two-column format and original diagrams and ablation displays remain.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the paper through an additional model-family evaluation, an explicit correctness check, clearer benchmarking and implementation disclosures, and corrections to numerical summaries and communication analysis. These improve confidence and reproducibility while retaining the original evidence. The gains are incremental: the larger headline speedup reflects newly evaluated Llama settings rather than a demonstrated improvement on the original workloads.
